description: Nurses’ Health Study II (NHS II) The Nurses’ Health Study II is a prospective cohort dataset that follows ≈ 116,000 U.S. registered nurses (ages 25‑42 at enrollment in 1989) through biennial questionnaires, biospecimen collections, and linked health‑record data. It was initiated by Dr. Walter Willett and colleagues at Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health (principal investigator) with NIH funding 【1†L1-L4】. The primary purpose is to investigate how diet, oral‑contraceptive use, hormonal factors, lifestyle, and environmental exposures influence the long‑term risk of chronic diseases (cancer, cardiovascular disease, diabetes, osteoporosis, neurodegeneration) and healthy aging among women 【1†L5-L7】. Researchers use the dataset to test etiologic hypotheses, develop risk‑prediction models, and explore gene‑environment interactions; it also underpins the Growing Up Today Study (GUTS), a second‑generation cohort that links offspring data to maternal exposures 【1†L9-L12】. Key features that distinguish NHS II include: * Large, well‑characterized female nursing cohort with >85 % follow‑up response rates every two years. * Extensive longitudinal data on diet, medication (especially oral contraceptives), reproductive history, physical activity, psychosocial factors, and biologic specimens (blood, urine). * Integration with national health registries and the ability to conduct inter‑generational analyses through GUTS. These attributes make NHS II one of the world’s richest resources for epidemiologic research on women’s health and chronic‑disease prevention.
